findings.summary: Lynx is a text-based, cross-platform web browser first released in 1992 by the University of Kansas. It renders web pages as plain text with numbered or cursor-highlighted links, supports core protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, Gopher, NNTP, WAIS), and can launch external handlers for non-text content. It does not natively support JavaScript or graphical elements like images and video, but offers privacy advantages by blocking web bugs. Lynx is highly configurable via command-line options, configuration files, and runtime menus, and remains in active maintenance. It is commonly used for accessibility, remote access, web crawling, and testing website performance over low-bandwidth or text-only environments.

mechanisms.title: Text-only rendering and link navigation
mechanisms.explanation: Lynx renders web pages as plain text, presenting links as highlighted items or numbered options that users select via cursor keys or number entry. This text-only approach avoids the need to render images or video natively.

mechanisms.title: Protocol handling via libwww fork
mechanisms.explanation: Lynx implements network protocol support using a fork of the libwww library, initially forked in 1996. This forked codebase handles Gopher, HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, NNTP, and WAIS, with HTTPS support added later as patches addressing encryption concerns.
